issues.description: The template's StockIngredient class defines a constructor with four parameters (String name, int price, int quantity, boolean strictValidation), whereas the problem statement UML and the solution expect a three-argument constructor StockIngredient(String, int, int). This mismatch will confuse students and prevent them from instantiating StockIngredient using the expected three-argument form (e.g., new StockIngredient(name, price, quantity)) when implementing SealSaloon or following examples.
issues.suggestedFix: Provide the expected three-argument constructor in the template (StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity)). Either add an overloaded 3-arg constructor that delegates to the existing 4-arg constructor or modify the existing constructor signature/implementation to match the 3-argument form described in the problem statement and used in the solution. This will align the template with the problem specification and the solution, avoiding compilation/usage errors for students.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML) and the solution use a StockIngredient constructor with signature StockIngredient(String, int, int), but the template's StockIngredient only provides StockIngredient(String, int, int, boolean). This mismatch in the constructor API (parameter list) creates a mapping and compilation problem for students: the exercise text and example usages expect a three-argument constructor, while the template forces a different four-argument constructor, increasing extraneous cognitive load and preventing straightforward implementation of SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery as described.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template StockIngredient API match the problem and solution by adding an overloaded constructor StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity) that delegates to the existing constructor (e.g., this(name, price, quantity, false)). Alternatively, update the problem text to require the four-argument constructor and show example usage accordingly. Preferably add the three-argument constructor to the template so students can instantiate StockIngredient(name, price, quantity) as described.
